What is the essential teaching in '15. More inspired words'?

In '15. More inspired words', the teaching opens with this observation: *"More inspired words]
“When you can separate the mind from its involvement with all things, the mind is no longer tied to sorrow."* The central invitation is to turn one's investigation inward — to verify the Dhamma not as a set of beliefs, but as directly observable reality in one's own body, speech, and mind. As the text teaches, the Dhamma is *akāliko* — ever-present — and *opanayiko* — leading inward — available to be known (*paccattaṁ*) by each practitioner for themselves. There is no need to search elsewhere; the truth is already here.
